verifications.claim: As of March 2026, Italian citizenship by descent (iure sanguinis) has been restricted.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'On Thursday the Constitutional Court said it would rule in favor of the government and its controversial 2025 law that restricted citizenship for those born abroad.' (March 2026 context); R2: 'On Thursday, March 12, Italy’s Constitutional Court signaled that it intends to uphold a controversial citizenship law'; R8: 'Italy’s Constitutional Court rejected constitutional challenges to Law 74/2025 on 12 March'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the Constitutional Court's March 2026 ruling upholding restrictions on jus sanguinis.

verifications.claim: Applicants must now generally prove a parent or grandparent was born in Italy and held exclusively Italian citizenship at the time of the descendant's birth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'only those with a parent or grandparent born in Italy will be recognized as citizens... must have held solely Italian citizenship at the time of their descendant’s birth'; R2: 'Only people with a parent or grandparent born in Italy will qualify... held only Italian citizenship when their child or grandchild was born'
verifications.reasoning: Exact match across sources on parent/grandparent born in Italy and exclusive Italian citizenship at descendant's birth.

verifications.claim: Previously unrestricted ancestry claims are limited.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Previously, Italians who moved abroad could pass citizenship to their children... meaning that citizenship... was passed down the generations'; R2: 'Under the previous system, Italian citizenship could pass down through generations... Long ancestral chains will no longer automatically transmit citizenship'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly contrast previous unlimited generations with new limits.

verifications.claim: Existing citizenship is unaffected.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'For those who already hold Italian citizenship, there is little indication that the ruling would strip them of their status. Ongoing citizenship applications are also not expected to be immediately impacted'; R1: implies no revocation for existing
verifications.reasoning: Direct statement in R2; R1 consistent.

verifications.claim: Applications submitted by March 27, 2025, are honored.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'the acceptance of applications... received... after 11.59 pm on 27 March 2025'; R7: 'submitted by 11:59 PM (Rome time) on March 27, 2025'; R8: 'following an application filed by 11:59 p.m. Rome time on 27 March 2025'
verifications.reasoning: Precise date match across official and news sources.

verifications.claim: The law limits recognition to applicants with a parent or grandparent born in Italy who held solely Italian citizenship at the time of the descendant’s birth (or at their own death if earlier).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'that parent or grandparent must have held solely Italian citizenship at the time of their descendant’s birth, or at their own death if it came earlier.'
verifications.reasoning: Exact phrasing and details match R1.

verifications.claim: If an Italian ancestor naturalized in another country before their child was born, the chain of citizenship is broken.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'prove that nobody in their ancestral line lost their citizenship'; R5: 'prove that their Italian-born ancestor did not obtain any additional citizenship... before the foreign-born child`s'; R7: 'certify that the Italian born ancestor... never naturalized... before the birth of the next generation'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state naturalization breaks the chain.

verifications.claim: The previous right of blood (jus sanguinis) allowed unlimited generational claims.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'citizenship... was passed down the generations'; R2: 'if you had an Italian ancestor... you could claim Italian citizenship, sometimes even several generations later... no limit to the number of descendants'
verifications.reasoning: Explicit description of prior unlimited generations.

verifications.claim: The previous right of blood (jus sanguinis) has been replaced with a strict parent/grandparent requirement.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'a law introduced on March 28 last year... states that only those with a parent or grandparent born in Italy'; R2: 'The new law tightens those rules considerably. Only people with a parent or grandparent born in Italy'
verifications.reasoning: Direct replacement described.

verifications.claim: Italian citizenship by descent (jure sanguinis) requires an uninterrupted line from a parent or grandparent born in Italy who did not naturalize elsewhere before the next generation's birth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'parent or grandparent born in Italy... must have held only Italian citizenship when their child or grandchild was born'; R5: 'their Italian-born ancestor did not obtain any additional citizenship... before the foreign-born child`s'
verifications.reasoning: Precise match on requirements.

verifications.claim: A foreign spouse of an Italian citizen can apply after 3 years of marriage if residing abroad.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'the application can be submitted three years after the marriage/civil union if the spouse is an Italian national'; R10: '3 years of matrimony if residing abroad'
verifications.reasoning: Exact timeframe for abroad residency.

verifications.claim: A foreign spouse of an Italian citizen can apply after 2 years if living in Italy.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R10: 'legal residence in Italy for at least 6 months after marriage'
verifications.reasoning: Sources specify 6 months (R10) or do not mention 2 years for Italy residency; claim's 2 years contradicts available info.

verifications.claim: The marriage period is reduced to 1.5 years if there are minor children.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'The three years are reduced to a year and a half if the couple has minor children'
verifications.reasoning: Direct match.

verifications.claim: Non-EU citizens can apply after 10 years of legal residency.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R10: 'Naturalisation requirements include: 10 years of legal residence'
verifications.reasoning: Exact match for non-EU naturalization.

verifications.claim: EU citizens can apply after 4 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R10: '4 years of legal residence for citizens of European Community Member States'
verifications.reasoning: Direct support.

verifications.claim: Individuals with parents or grandparents born in Italy may apply after 2 years of legal residency.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R10: 'If the foreigner is of Italian descent (up to the 2nd degree)... by residing legally in Italy for at least two years after reaching legal age'
verifications.reasoning: Matches 2nd degree (parent/grandparent) and 2 years residency.

verifications.claim: Birth certificates, marriage certificates, and death certificates for every person in the direct line are required, translated into Italian and legalized (e.g., with an Apostille).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'source birth, marriage and death certificates... (which can take years)'; R7: 'Birth certificates... Marriage certificate... Death certificates... duly legalized and translated into Italian'; R4: details apostille and translation
verifications.reasoning: Standard requirements explicitly listed.

verifications.claim: Official proof is required that the Italian-born ancestor did not become a naturalized citizen of their new country before the birth of the next generation.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'prove that their Italian-born ancestor did not obtain any additional citizenship... before the foreign-born child`s'; R7: 'certify that the Italian born ancestor who emigrated never naturalized... In case your ancestor... naturalized abroad, the applicant must also submit a notarized copy'
verifications.reasoning: Precise requirement stated.

verifications.claim: Applications are generally handled through Italian consulates abroad or directly in Italy through residency.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'make an appointment online through... Prenot@mi'; R9: 'apply for Italian citizenship by descent in Italy... through the citizenship office'; R10: 'presented to the Prefecture... if residing in Italy, or the diplomatic-consular authorities if residing abroad'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm consulates abroad or comune/prefecture in Italy.

verifications.claim: Children of Italian-born women born before 1948 previously needed to file a lawsuit to claim citizenship.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'descendants of Italian women who gave birth before then are blocked from recognition. Since 2009 many have successfully sued the state for gender discrimination'
verifications.reasoning: Direct historical requirement via lawsuit.

verifications.claim: Women could not transmit citizenship prior to 1948.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'women were not able to transmit citizenship until 1948'; R5: 'If there is a woman in the line of descent, Italian citizenship can be transmitted only if the son/daughter was born after January 1, 1948'
verifications.reasoning: Explicit pre-1948 restriction.

verifications.claim: New rules allow voluntary acquisition of citizenship for minors if a parent is an Italian citizen by birth and declares intent within a specific timeframe.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R12: 'A minor may acquire Italian citizenship if: at least one parent is an Italian citizen by birth; both parents submit a declaration of intent... within one year of the child’s birth'
verifications.reasoning: Matches new provisions for minors via parental declaration.
